taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, reasoning allowed. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To calculate the deadline:

1. **Target Date:** "Six days from Saturday, October 24, 2026" is Friday, October 30, 2026.
2. **Time Conversion:** The deadline is 11:59 PM PT (Pacific Time) on October 30. Madrid is in the Central European Time (CET) zone. On October 30, 2026, Madrid is still in Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2. Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) is UTC-7. 
3. **Time Difference:** The difference between CEST (UTC+2) and PDT (UTC-7) is 9 hours. 
4. **Calculation:** 23:59 (11:59 PM) + 9 hours = 08:59 on the following day (October 31).

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline, we first establish the timeline:

1.  **The Deadline:** Monday, November 2, 2026, at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time (Pacific Standard Time/PST).
2.  **Time Difference:** On November 2, 2026, Los Angeles is in PST (UTC-8). Madrid is in CET (UTC+1). Therefore, Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles.
3.  **Calculation:** 10:00 AM Monday + 9 hours = 7:00 PM (19:00) on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the end time of the hackathon, we follow these steps:

1.  **Start Time:** Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 18:00.
2.  **Duration:** 48 hours is exactly two full days.
3.  **Calculation:** Adding 2 days to Saturday, October 24, 2026, results in Monday, October 26, 2026. The time remains the same (18:00).
4.  **Time Zone:** Since you are in Madrid and the event is defined in "Madrid time," your local time is identical to the event time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline, we first establish the timeline:

1.  **Start time:** October 26, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT (Pacific Time).
2.  **Duration:** 72 hours (exactly 3 days).
3.  **End time (PT):** October 29, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT.
4.  **Time Zone Conversion:** On October 29, 2026, the United States is observing Pacific Standard Time (PST), which is UTC-8. Madrid, Spain, is observing Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1.
5.  **Calculation:** The time difference between PST (UTC-8) and CET (UTC+1) is 9 hours. Therefore, 10:00 AM PT + 9 hours = 19:00 (7:00 PM) in Madrid.

(Note: Daylight Saving Time ends in Europe on October 25, 2026, and in the US on November 1, 2026, so the 9-hour difference holds for this date.)

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the exact time in Madrid, let's break down the conversion:

1.  **Submission Deadline:** October 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET.
2.  **Add 36 hours:**
    *   36 hours is equal to 24 hours + 12 hours.
    *   Adding 24 hours to Oct 31, 11:59 PM brings us to Nov 1, 11:59 PM ET.
    *   Adding the remaining 12 hours brings us to Nov 2, 2026, at 11:59 AM ET.
3.  **Time Zone Adjustment:**
    *   Madrid is on Central European Time (CET). On November 2, 2026, daylight saving time (CEST) will have ended in Europe (it ends on the last Sunday of October).
    *   In November, Madrid is UTC+1, while Eastern Time (ET) is Eastern Standard Time (EST), which is UTC-5.
    *   The time difference is 6 hours (Madrid is 6 hours ahead of ET).
4.  **Conversion:**
    *   11:59 AM ET + 6 hours = 5:59 PM (17:59) local time in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 17:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the Unix timestamp 1791788340 to local time in Tokyo:

1.  A Unix timestamp of 1791788340 seconds since the epoch (January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC) corresponds to **Wednesday, December 10, 2037, at 07:59:00 UTC**.
2.  Tokyo is in Japan Standard Time (JST), which is UTC+9.
3.  Adding 9 hours to 07:59:00 UTC results in 16:59:00 JST.

ANSWER: 2037-12-10 16:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is given in UTC (indicated by the "Z"). 

Madrid, Spain, is in the Central European Time (CET) zone. On October 25, 2026, Spain will be observing Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.

To convert the time:
1. 2026-10-25 02:30 UTC
2. Add 2 hours for CEST: 02:30 + 2:00 = 04:30.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 04:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline, we look at the specific date and time:

1.  **Date:** The last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25, 2026.
2.  **Time:** 11:59 PM (23:59) Pacific Time (PT).
3.  **Time Zone Difference:** In late October, Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) is UTC-7. Madrid, Spain, is in Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.
4.  **Conversion:** Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Pacific Time (2 + 7 = 9).
5.  **Calculation:** Adding 9 hours to October 25, 2026, at 23:59 results in October 26, 2026, at 08:59. (Note: On this date, both regions are still observing their respective daylight saving times).

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 08:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline, we look at the following facts:

1.  **US Daylight Saving Time (DST) 2026:** In the United States, DST ends on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, that date is **November 1, 2026**.
2.  **Time Zone Conversion:** On November 1, 2026, the US will have transitioned from Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4) to Eastern Standard Time (EST, UTC-5). 
3.  **Lima Time:** Lima, Peru, operates on Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5 throughout the entire year.
4.  **The Calculation:** At 12:00 noon EST (UTC-5) on November 1, 2026, the time in Lima (also UTC-5) will be exactly the same.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

"AoE" stands for "Anywhere on Earth," which is equivalent to UTC-12. When it is 24:00 (midnight) at the end of December 31, 2026, in the UTC-12 time zone, it is exactly the start of January 1, 2027, in UTC.

Tokyo (JST) is UTC+9. Therefore, when it becomes January 1, 2027, 00:00 UTC, it is 09:00 AM on the same day in Tokyo.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 09:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in New York time, we must account for the time difference between Sydney and New York on October 5, 2026.

1. **Time Zones:** Sydney (AEDT) is UTC+11 during daylight saving time (which begins on October 4, 2026). New York (EDT) is UTC-4.
2. **Difference:** The time difference between Sydney (UTC+11) and New York (UTC-4) is 15 hours. Sydney is 15 hours ahead of New York.
3. **Calculation:**
   *   Deadline: October 5, 2026, 17:00 (5:00 PM) Sydney time.
   *   Subtract 15 hours: 17:00 - 15 hours = 02:00 (2:00 AM) on the same day.

The deadline is October 5, 2026, at 2:00 AM New York time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
